model_interpretation.claim: A conventional 32x33 padded shared tile with 32x8 threads should preserve coalesced input loads and output stores while avoiding the XOR indexing of the prior 32x32 swizzled variant. model_interpretation.claim: A 32x32 shared tile indexed as tile[row][col ^ row] provides a meaningful alternative to the padded 32x33 scalar layout: it preserves coalesced global loads/stores while avoiding padding, and may avoid shared-memory bank conflicts on a 32-bank organization. model_interpretation.claim: A 32x33 padded shared tile with 8x32 threads, each owning four adjacent input and output values, may improve on the prior scalar-ownership variants by using aligned 16-byte global transfers and fewer per-element global instructions. Integer bit-pattern transfers avoid floating-point arithmetic. The supplied measurements make XOR-swizzled scalar ownership a slightly faster comparison point than padded scalar ownership, but neither result predicts this vectorized variant's performance.
